nodes.text: But the queen—for the sick are somehow inclined to lend an ear to ill-omened things—took the accusation to be true, especially as it had come from Jews; for she shared their views and lived in the Jewish manner, and thought them truthful and well-disposed to her. And the Magi, taking Tarbula and the other women, condemn them to death; and having cut them in two with a saw, they impaled them on stakes, and, as a charm to avert the sickness, [made] the queen pass through between the stakes

And at last they made a wooden tripod of laurel, and consecrated [it] with the invocations and formulas to which they were accustomed, so that, by the gathering of letters, each letter being indicated by the device of the tripod and by the divination, the name of the future emperor might be revealed.
